1.title: Context Management and Large Codebase Exploration
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Context Management and Large Codebase Exploration. This module covers task statements five point one and five point four: context management and large codebase exploration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Progressive summarization risks and the "case facts" block. The "lost in the middle" effect and how to place information. How tool results swell the context, and how to trim them. Context degradation in long sessions, scratchpad files, subagent delegation, manifests and slash compact.

1.title: Case Check-In: Birchwood Supply's Long Support Chat
1.text: Our running case is Birchwood Supply. Birchwood Supply's Long Support Chat. A customer chats for an hour about three issues: a late order, a duplicate charge and a damaged item. After several summarizations, the agent forgets the exact refund amount (eighty-four dollars and fifty cents), the promised date (twelve March) and which order goes with which problem. Each lookup order call returns forty plus fields, but only five matter for returns.

1.title: Keeping Critical Facts Alive
1.text: Keeping Critical Facts Alive. Progressive summarization. What happens: Numbers, percentages, dates and customer-stated expectations become vague ("a refund was discussed"). Remedy: Keep transactional facts in a persistent "case facts" block outside the summarized history, included in every prompt. Multi-issue sessions. What happens: Facts of different issues blend together. Remedy: Extract structured issue data (order I Ds, amounts, statuses) into a separate context layer. Tool-result bloat. What happens: forty plus fields per lookup eat tokens out of proportion to their value. Remedy: Trim each result to the relevant fields before it accumulates.

1.title: Keeping Critical Facts Alive, continued
1.text: Keeping Critical Facts Alive, continued. "Lost in the middle". What happens: Models reliably use the beginning and end of a long input but may omit findings from the middle. Remedy: Put a key-findings summary at the start; organize details under explicit section headers. Context limits of downstream agents. What happens: A verbose upstream result overruns the next agent. Remedy: Have upstream agents return structured data (key facts, citations, relevance scores) instead of long text and reasoning chains. Lost provenance. What happens: Synthesis cannot tell where facts came from. Remedy: Require subagents to include metadata (dates, source locations, methodological context) in structured outputs.

1.text: Keeping Critical Facts Alive, continued. The A P I (application programming interface) is stateless: to keep a conversation coherent you must send the complete conversation history (plus your case-facts block) in each request to maintain conversational coherence.

1.text: Keeping Critical Facts Alive, continued. The figure shows this: Position matters in long inputs: put the key findings first and structure the rest with headers so nothing is lost in the middle. Exam tip: Customer's exact amounts and dates keep disappearing? to a persistent case-facts block outside the summary. Do not "summarize more carefully". Exam tip: Exact amounts and dates lost in a long chat call for a case-facts block outside the summary, not "summarize better".

1.title: Exploring Large Codebases
1.text: Exploring Large Codebases. Case (continued): An engineer explores Birchwood's three thousand-file monorepo for hours. After a while Claude begins to say "this probably uses the typical repository pattern" instead of naming the specific classes it found earlier. Context degradation: in extended sessions the model gives inconsistent answers and refers to "typical patterns" instead of the specific classes discovered earlier.

1.title: Exploring Large Codebases, continued
1.text: Exploring Large Codebases, continued. Scratchpad files. The agent writes key findings to a file and references it for subsequent questions, so facts survive context boundaries. Subagent delegation. Spawn subagents for specific questions ("find all test files", "trace the refund flow's dependencies"); the verbose output stays in their context and the main agent keeps high-level coordination. Phase summaries. Summarize key findings of one phase before spawning subagents for the next, and inject the summary into their initial context.

1.title: Exploring Large Codebases, continued
1.text: Exploring Large Codebases, continued. State manifests (crash recovery). Each agent exports its state to a known location; the coordinator loads a manifest on resume and injects the state into agent prompts. slash compact. Reduces context usage when it fills with verbose discovery output.

1.title: Exploring Large Codebases, continued
1.text: Exploring Large Codebases, continued. The figure shows this: Large exploration: delegate verbose searching to subagents, record findings in a scratchpad, and keep a manifest so a crashed run can resume. Current documentation: a subagent returns only its final message to the parent, so its detailed tool calls stay out of the parent's context; when the context window nears its limit, Claude Code and the Agent S D K (software development kit) compact automatically (older turns are summarized), and instructions that must persist belong in Claude dot M D, which is re-loaded. As of eight November two thousand twenty-six. Exam tip: Long exploration drifting to "typical patterns" calls for a scratchpad file and subagents, and slash compact when verbose output fills the context.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Summarization risk: Amounts, dates, expectations get vague to case-facts block outside the summary. Multi-issue: Separate structured issue layer. Tool output: Trim to relevant fields (five of forty plus ). Position effect: Beginning and end are reliable; middle is not to summary first plus section headers. Upstream agents: Return structured facts, citations, relevance scores, with metadata (dates, sources). Statelessness: Send the complete history each request. Degradation: "Typical patterns" instead of specific classes to scratchpad, subagents, phase summaries. Recovery: State exports plus manifest loaded by the coordinator on resume. slash compact: Reduce context when verbose discovery fills it.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. After many turns, Birchwood's agent forgets the exact refund amount and a promised date because earlier turns were summarized. What is the best fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Transactional facts must not pass through progressive summarization.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A customer discusses three issues in one chat, and the agent mixes up which order has which problem. What helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. A separate structured layer keeps each issue's facts distinct.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An order lookup returns forty plus fields, but only five are relevant for returns, and the context fills quickly. What is the best approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Trimming keeps relevant data and prevents token waste.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An aggregated research input of thirty findings is passed to a synthesis agent, which tends to omit findings from the middle. What mitigates this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Models attend best to the start and end; a summary first and clear headers reduce loss in the middle.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A subagent returns paragraphs of reasoning, but the downstream synthesis agent has a small context budget. What should change? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Structured, compact upstream output fits a limited downstream budget while keeping attribution.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. During a long exploration, the agent starts to answer with "typical patterns" rather than the specific classes it found earlier. Which combination counters this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Persisting findings and isolating verbose output keep specifics available and context lean.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Select two. Which two practices keep critical facts alive in a long support conversation? The five options are on the screen. The answers are D and E. Verbatim facts and lean tool output protect important details. Heavier summarization and bloated results make things worse.

1.title: Practice Question 8
1.text: Question eight. Select two. Which two help counter context degradation in a long codebase exploration? The five options are on the screen. The answers are D and E. Persisting findings and isolating verbose exploration keep specifics available and context small.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all eight answers. Question one: A. Question two: A. Question three: C. Question four: D. Question five: B. Question six: C. Question seven: D and E. Question eight: D and E. In the next module, we continue the course.
